text.p: French retail group Pinault-Printemps-Redoute reported on Wednesday that its profits rose sharply in 1996, in line with analysts' expectations.
Net attributable profit rose 36.2 percent to 2.07 billion francs ($364.2 million) from 1.52 billion francs in 1995 on a 3.6 percent rise in sales to 80.39 billion francs.
Analysts had forecast a profit of 2.05 billion francs.

Operating profit at the group, whose retailers include department store Printemps and music and books chain FNAC, rose 18.4 percent to 3.54 billion francs, helped by productivity gains and slower growth in operating costs.
Lower interest rates helped slash its financial expense to 221 million francs from 554 million, Pinault-Printemps said in a statement.
It said sales in the first two months of 1997 were up six percent.
"Despite a general trend of weak consumption comparable to that seen in the second half of 1996, the group's stores are increasing their shares of the market," the statement said.

Pinault-Printemps shares rose 2.45 percent to 2,302 francs on Wednesday before the results, which were announced after the stock market closed. One trader said the share was looking undervalued, relative to the market's gains. ($ = 5.683 French Francs)
